deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous and next pages): Hilbert is sketching a new proof of 'meinen Satz über Nomographie'. This is his claim, tied to his 13th Problem and announced in print in 1927 without proof, that there exist analytic functions f(x,y,z) of three variables that cannot be obtained by finitely many superpositions of analytic functions of two variables. Earlier he proved it 'by counting coefficients of power series'. Here he proposes a PDE method: each superposition scheme forces f to satisfy a nontrivial PDE.

The scheme is level by level, with n = 3 levels.
- Level 1: x1 = x1(y,z), y1 = y1(x,z). These satisfy (1): (x1)_x = 0, (y1)_y = 0.
- Previous page: any w(x1,y1) has w_x = w_{y1}(y1)_x, w_y = w_{x1}(x1)_y and w_z = w_{x1}(x1)_z + w_{y1}(y1)_z. Eliminating w_{x1} and w_{y1} gives w_z = ((x1)_z/(x1)_y) w_y + ((y1)_z/(y1)_x) w_x. This needs (x1)_y ≠ 0 and (y1)_x ≠ 0, which is implicit.

This page.
- Level 2: put x2 = x2(x1,y1), y2 = y2(x1,y1). Applying the identity above with w = x2 and w = y2 gives system (2):
  (x2)_z = ((x1)_z/(x1)_y)(x2)_y + ((y1)_z/(y1)_x)(x2)_x,
  (y2)_z = ((x1)_z/(x1)_y)(y2)_y + ((y1)_z/(y1)_x)(y2)_x.
- For an arbitrary w(x2,y2), the chain rule gives grad w = w_{x2} grad x2 + w_{y2} grad y2. So the three gradients are linearly dependent, i.e. det[[w_x,(x2)_x,(y2)_x],[w_y,(x2)_y,(y2)_y],[w_z,(x2)_z,(y2)_z]] = 0. Hilbert writes 'z' instead of w_z in the last row (slip).
- Level 3: x3 = x3(x2,y2), y3 = y3(x2,y2). These satisfy system (3): the same 3x3 determinant with first column grad x3, respectively grad y3, equals 0.
- Conclusion: f is producible by 3-fold application of suitable two-argument functions iff f, together with suitably chosen x1,y1,x2,y2,x3,y3 as functions of x,y,z, satisfies 7 PDEs. These are (1) [2 eqs], (2) [2], (3) [2] and, on the next page, (4) det[grad f, grad x3, grad y3] = 0 [1]; 2+2+2+1 = 7.
- Next page: a non-degeneracy condition is required, namely that not all 2x2 minors of the last two columns vanish. Elimination of the six auxiliary functions should give a genuine resultant PDE F_n(f) = 0. One then takes an entire power series P(x,y,z) satisfying none of the countably many F_n = 0.

What is mine: the explicit gradient-dependence justification of the determinant and the equation count are my fillings.
errors: In the determinant for w(x2,y2) the bottom-left entry is written 'z'; it must be w_z. As written the determinant does not vanish in general.
Hilbert writes 'Funktion' where the plural is meant ('geeigneten Funktionen von nur 2 Argumenten'); this is cosmetic.
Derivation of (2) silently assumes (x1)_y ≠ 0 and (y1)_x ≠ 0; dividing by these is unjustified in degenerate cases.
Equations (1)-(4) are only necessary conditions. The converse needs a rank condition on (grad x2, grad y2) and (grad x3, grad y3), which Hilbert adds only on the next page.
The key step, that eliminating the auxiliary functions yields a nontrivial equation F_n(f) = 0, is left unproved. Hilbert himself flags it ('Aufstellung eines geeigneten allgemeinen Kriteriums...').
The specific level-1 pattern (x1(y,z), y1(x,z)) does not obviously cover every superposition tree; a full argument must range over all (countably many) schemes.
Next page, eq. (4): the first column is written (f_x)_x, (f_y)_y, (f_z)_z; it should be f_x, f_y, f_z.

results.what: Functions obtained from two-variable inner functions satisfy first-order linear PDEs. Level 1: x1(y,z), y1(x,z) satisfy (x1)_x = 0, (y1)_y = 0. Any w(x1,y1) satisfies w_z = (x1_z/x1_y) w_y + (y1_z/y1_x) w_x.
results.modern_name: Characterization of functions of given functions via gradient dependence (functional dependence / Jacobian criterion)

results.what: f(x3,y3) with x3, y3 functions of x,y,z holds iff det[grad f, grad x3, grad y3] = 0 (with rank-2 nondegeneracy).

Strategy: encode an n-level superposition scheme as an overdetermined PDE system (7 equations for n = 3), eliminate the auxiliaries to get a resultant PDE F_n(f) = 0, then choose an entire function avoiding all countably many F_n. This would prove existence of analytic functions of 3 variables not representable by finite superpositions of analytic functions of 2 variables.
results.modern_name: Differential-algebraic (resultant PDE) approach to Hilbert's 13th problem in the analytic category; 'differential-equation obstruction to superposition'
results.usually_credited_to: Claim announced by Hilbert (1927, 'Über die Gleichung neunten Grades'). Related differential-equation obstructions: Ostrowski (1920). Analytic non-representability later treated by Vitushkin and others.

deep.surprise_reason: Hilbert's claim to have proved the analytic non-representability theorem is known from his 1927 paper, as is the fact that his proof was by power-series coefficient counting. This page adds an unpublished alternative proof sketch via elimination from an overdetermined PDE system plus a countability argument. That is a notable but incomplete detail; the decisive nontriviality of the elimination is not established here.

checkable.sympy: x,y,z=symbols('x y z'); A=Function('A')(y,z); B=Function('B')(x,z); G=Function('G')(A,B); simplify(diff(G,z) - diff(A,z)/diff(A,y)*diff(G,y) - diff(B,z)/diff(B,x)*diff(G,x)) == 0
checkable.asserts: Equation (2): any x2 = G(x1,y1) with x1 = A(y,z), y1 = B(x,z) satisfies (x2)_z = (x1_z/x1_y)(x2)_y + (y1_z/y1_x)(x2)_x.

checkable.sympy: x,y,z=symbols('x y z'); P=Function('P')(x,y,z); Q=Function('Q')(x,y,z); W=Function('W')(P,Q); simplify(Matrix([[diff(W,v),diff(P,v),diff(Q,v)] for v in (x,y,z)]).det()) == 0
checkable.asserts: Determinant equation on the page (and system (3), eq. (4)): for w = W(x2,y2), det[grad w, grad x2, grad y2] = 0.

checkable.sympy: x,y,z=symbols('x y z'); P=x+y**2; Q=y*z; W=sin(P)*Q; simplify(Matrix([[diff(W,x),diff(P,x),diff(Q,x)],[diff(W,y),diff(P,y),diff(Q,y)],[z,diff(P,z),diff(Q,z)]]).det()) != 0
checkable.asserts: Hilbert's literal entry 'z' (instead of w_z) gives a nonzero determinant, so it is a slip.

checkable.sympy: x,y,z=symbols('x y z'); A=Function('A')(y,z); B=Function('B')(x,z); (diff(A,x), diff(B,y)) == (0,0)

transcription_corrections: Bottom-left entry of the w-determinant is indeed written 'z' in the image; the transcription is faithful, but mathematically it should be w_z.
'von [-Fun-] geeigneten Funktion' — the image shows 'Fun' struck and 'geeigneten Funktion' written; the sense is plural.
The deletion after 'nach' looks like a struck '3fa'/'3f'; the transcription is plausible.
The deletions transcribed as '(3)' after 'Anwendung' and after 'erzeugen' look in the image like struck '(f3)'/'f3' marks rather than '(3)'.
In (2), the first denominator shows a struck 'y' before (x1)_y, and the second denominator (y1)_x has a struck 'y' subscript before x. Both are correctly rendered.
